description: A single-panel X-ray photoelectron spectrum, labelled "(a₂)", showing the Al 2p region. The x-axis is printed "Binding energy (eV)" with ticks every 2 eV from 82 (left) down to 66 (right); the y-axis is "Intensity (a.u.)" with no numeric scale printed. The raw data are a noisy blue trace dominated by one broad asymmetric peak whose maximum lies just above the 74 eV gridline; a black arrow points at this peak and labels it "Al³⁺". A smooth red curve is overlaid as the fitted envelope, and the area beneath the main peak is shaded pink-to-purple, marking the fitted Al³⁺ component. A second, much weaker orange curve branches off the right flank of the peak and decays towards about 70-68 eV, representing a background or minor fitted component. The spectrum therefore indicates that aluminium at the probed surface exists predominantly in the oxidised Al³⁺ state (consistent with an Al-rich surface oxide film) rather than as metallic Al. No intensity values, component percentages, fitting parameters or acquisition conditions are printed; the "(a₂)" tag implies this panel is one sub-image of a larger composite figure of which only this piece was supplied.

observations.observation: The panel is an XPS spectrum with x-axis labelled 'Binding energy (eV)' and y-axis 'Intensity (a.u.)'.
The x-axis tick scale runs from 82 eV at the left to 66 eV at the right in 2 eV steps.
One dominant broad peak is present, its maximum lying between the 76 and 72 eV gridlines, closest to the 74 eV tick.
An arrow annotation labels the main peak 'Al³⁺'.
A smooth red curve is drawn over the noisy raw data as a fitted envelope, and the region under the main peak is shaded pink-purple to denote the fitted Al³⁺ component.
A second, much weaker orange curve follows the lower flank of the peak and decays towards ~68-70 eV, representing a background or minor component.
No numeric intensity values are printed on the y-axis and no component percentages or fitting parameters appear on the panel.
The peak position near 74 eV and the 'Al³⁺' assignment indicate aluminium is present mainly in the oxidised state at the analysed surface.
The panel tag '(a₂)' indicates this spectrum is one sub-image of a larger multi-panel figure; only this panel was supplied and no caption was extracted.

subfigures.description: XPS Al 2p spectrum plotted as Intensity (a.u.) versus Binding energy (eV) from 82 to 66 eV; a single broad peak centred near 74 eV is arrow-labelled 'Al³⁺'. Raw noisy data (blue), a red fitted envelope, a pink-purple shaded Al³⁺ component, and a weaker orange curve on the high-binding-energy/lower flank are visible.
